articles.title: ‘Broke people get screwed’: the shameful history of crime and punishment in America
articles.summary: An eight-hour docuseries looks back to explore the many problems and injustices that have helped to further break a broken system Lynn Novick’s new film for PBS is an epic, an eight-hour examination of Crime & Punishment in America . Beginning with justice in tribal societies, the documentary follows the arc of US history and ends in today’s troubled prison system, with the story of a podcast produced by prisoners in San Quentin and scenes from Rikers Island . “I’ve been working with Ken Burns on films about American history for all of my career, basically, and looked at the story of America through many different perspectives,” Novick said. “And honestly, I had never paid that much attention to the question of the justice system until 14 years ago, I had the opportunity to teach, to do a guest lecture in a college class inside a prison.”

articles.title: ‘Mick Jagger should fold up his penis and go home’: the caustic genius of music critic Robert Christgau
articles.summary: Beloved for his savage takedowns and rhapsodic raves, the legendary Village Voice reviewer opens up in a candid new documentary Rows and rows of CDs, albums, cassettes and books creak and groan on shelves that snake around the walls and choke the halls of an apartment in New York City’s East Village. The clutter that sprawls through its rooms is so dense it suggests the twistiest parts of a Moroccan medina or a warren no self-respecting rabbit would allow. Buried amid the muddle is a man hunched over a computer keyboard, clacking out words meant to make sense of all the sounds that this physical media holds. articles.title: Call my (estate) agent! Why celebrities are always buying each other’s homes
articles.summary: If you’re seeking a discreet mansion with secluded grounds and plenty of room for your own memorabilia, you may want to remember Joe Pesci’s mistakes before trying the open market Last year, Austin Butler bought a mansion from Brad Pitt. The month before, Brad Pitt bought a mansion from one of the Killers. In 2022, Adele bought Sylvester Stallone’s old house, but only if he let her keep his Rocky statue. Aaron Paul recently sold a house that he bought from The Big Bang Theory’s Jim Parsons, who bought it from Robert Pattinson, after it was previously owned by Noah Wyle, Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, Tim Curry and the guy who directed Legally Blonde.
